{{Short description|Annual association football award event in France}} {{Infobox award | name = 2003 Ballon d'Or | image = Pavel Nedvěd.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = 2003 Ballon d'Or winner, Pavel Nedvěd | date = 22 December 2003 | location = | presenter = ''[[France Football]]'' | host = | website = {{URL|ballondor.com}} | award1_type = Won by | award1_winner = {{flagicon|CZE}} [[Pavel Nedvěd]] (1st award) | award2_type = | award2_winner = | award3_type = | award3_winner = | award4_type = | award4_winner = | award5_type = | award5_winner = | previous = [[2002 Ballon d'Or|2002]] | main = [[Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[2004 Ballon d'Or|2004]] }} The '''2003 Ballon d'Or''' ({{lit|'''2003 Golden Ball'''}}), given to the best [[Association football|football]] player in Europe as judged by a panel of sports journalists from [[UEFA]] member countries, was awarded to the [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[midfielder]] [[Pavel Nedvěd]] on 22 December 2003.{{cite web |last= BBC Sport staff | url = http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3341645.stm | title = Nedved scoops top award | date = 22 December 2003 | work = [[BBC Sport]] }} Nedvěd was the second Czech player to win the award after [[Josef Masopust]] ([[1962 Ballon d'Or|1962]]). [[Gianluigi Buffon]] (Italy) was the top ranked goalkeeper in the list, in ninth place. [[Paolo Maldini]] (Italy) was the best ranked [[Defender (association football)|defender]] in third place, while [[Thierry Henry]] (France) was the top [[Forward (association football)|forward]], in second place. ==Rankings== On 11 November 2003, the shortlist of 50 male players compiled by a group of experts from ''[[France Football]]'' was announced.{{Cite news |last=UEFA.com |title=Short list reflects Madrid lustre {{!}} UEFA Champions League 2003/04 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0eaad1af0fdc-870e00cd2160-1000--short-list-reflects-madrid-lustre/ 52 voters, from Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, England, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Macedonia, Malta, Moldova, the Netherlands, Northern Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Ireland, Romania, Russia, San Marino, Scotland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, Ukraine, Wales and [[FR Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]. Each picked a first (5pts), second (4pts), third (3pts), fourth (2pts) and fifth choice (1pt).{{cite web |last= Pierrend |first= José | url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy03.html | title = European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 2003 | date = 26 March 2005 | work = [[RSSSF]] }} ===Voted players=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size: 90%; text-align: center;" |- !
